set.body:
Objective
Make Ravel broadly fast on public workloads while preserving exact ndarray semantics, typed ownership, deterministic behavior, C-order allocation contracts, and JVM/Scala.js portability. This epic continues from the closed NumPy frontier receipts; it does not reopen completed work.

Principles
- Optimize reusable semantic classes, never benchmark names, fixed shapes, or one-off parameter tuples.
- Measure public APIs with semantic and layout signatures, allocation evidence, and visible losses.
- Require witnesses across sizes, dtypes, contiguous and offset-contiguous inputs, broadcasting, inner and outer striding, transpose, and reversal where applicable.
- Dispatch outside hot loops and keep inner loops monomorphic. Any new abstraction must compile or lower to a direct loop, not a per-element callback or interpreter.
- Preserve exact pairwise reduction semantics and all existing NaN, Boolean, alias, overlap, broadcasting, and ownership laws.
- Treat JVM Vector API and parallel execution as optional capability layers with scalar and serial fallbacks.

Cross-platform proof policy
Every shared-kernel change must pass JVM and Scala.js laws, Scala.js fullLink, and matched semantic signatures. Scala.js performance is measured against a same-host, pinned-Node baseline, not against NumPy running in another runtime. Browser performance is diagnostic until its variance is characterized; browser correctness remains mandatory. JVM-only SIMD must not enter shared core or weaken Scala.js. Node and browser JavaScript remain serial unless a separately justified Worker design proves transfer and coordination costs worthwhile. Scala.js Long remains correctness-only unless its storage contract changes explicitly.

Performance policy
The first child freezes reproducible baselines. A focused optimization normally needs at least a 1.20x improvement on its targeted class, no unexplained regression above 10 percent on any established public case, exact signature parity, and no size-proportional allocation beyond required results or documented workspaces. Final closeout reruns the broad JVM NumPy court and the Scala.js court on a calm host, reports geomeans plus every visible loss, and records accepted no-go decisions as evidence rather than hiding them.

Exit
All child decisions and implementations are closed with receipts; the final court shows which gaps were removed, which remain structurally attributable to runtime or semantics, and whether the next marginal optimization is justified.
set.title: EPIC: Close the Ravel performance gap without contract loss
